messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1743201234 - p99 latency breach on dedicated 'hotshot-eu' pool. Objective: paging SLO breach (p95/p99), streaming stalls observed. Auto-escalation to #incidents.
Alex: Paging in — I'm oncall. Seeing alert: p99 jumped to ~4.8s last 5m, p95 ~1.6s. Streaming sessions showing stalls/partial chunks.
Maya: Confirming telemetry — queue depth for hotshot-eu increased from ~20 -> ~620 in 2m. Warmup queue backed up. Autoscaler logs show repeated handshake timeouts with the warmup agent.
Joe: Noted. Recent runtime change adjusted handshake TTL from 10s -> 6s (optimization). That may be too aggressive for cold kernels under load.
Lina: Support: two customers reported degraded streaming UX (customer-phi, babel-ai). Tickets incoming, we should mark status page.
Alex: Immediate question: can we add capacity manually and/or route to fallback region?
Maya: I can attempt manual scale up of the pool and increase handshake TTL temporarily. Trying commands now.
Maya: ```bash
# manual scale
rictl pools scale --pool hotshot-eu --count 6
# adjust handshake
rictl config set --pool hotshot-eu --handshake-ttl 15
```
Maya: Running `scale` — looks like API returning 202 but provisioning is slowed due to warmup backlog (instances stuck in WARMUP). Logs show warmup failures referencing kernel init timeouts.
Joe: Paste from warmup agent log: ```
[2026-03-14T22:01:12Z] warmup-agent hotshot-eu instance-32: kernel_load_timeout after 9.8s
[2026-03-14T22:01:13Z] warmup-agent: retrying preheat kv-cache (0/3)
[2026-03-14T22:01:14Z] warmup-agent: handshake failed to complete, aborting
```
Alex: So autoscaler is requesting nodes but warmup can't finish, so they never enter Ready pool -> queue continues to grow. That's the warmup bottleneck.
Ron: Any quick mitigations? Can we bypass warmup for a subset of instances (hotshot) to allow bare-bones readiness? Risky but might reduce queue.
Joe: Two practical mitigations: 1) Increase handshake TTL & allow nodes longer preheat window (low-risk), 2) Provision hot spare instances with minimal model variant (quantized, smaller KV) and serve degraded-but-functional outputs to reduce p99.
Maya: I've increased handshake TTL to 15s and bumped pool desired count by 4. Also temporarily disabled aggressive kernel pruning in warmup-agent config.
Maya: ```bash
rictl config set --pool hotshot-eu --warmup-prune false
rictl pools scale --pool hotshot-eu --count 10
```
Lina: Noted, telling support to update customers: "investigating a temporary performance regression due to capacity warmup; engineering is scaling and applying mitigations."
Sam: Can we enable routing fallback to hosted API for affected customers? That reduces guarantees but gets them responsive. We should offer opt-in failover.
Joe: I can flip route policy for customer-phi and babel-ai to hosted fallback until pool stabilizes. Doing patch to routing rules now.
Joe: ```json
{
  "route": "customer-phi",
  "fallback": "hosted-latency-optimized",
  "max_tokens": 2048
}
```
Alex: Any metrics after the config changes?
Maya: After scaling commands: pool showing new instances registering but ~60% still in WARMUP. Queue depth trending down (620 -> 240 over 6m). p99 dropped from 4.8s -> 2.2s but still above SLO. Streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated.
Ron: We should watch for tail latency recurrence once the warmup drain completes — might see a second wave when other pools attempt to absorb traffic.
Joe: Root cause hypothesis: handshake TTL lowered in recent runtime change combined with heavier kernel init times for quantized models under new kernel selection. Autoscaler considered nodes unhealthy (handshake failures) and kept retrying -> warmup starvation.
Alex: Customer impact summary for paging: p95 breached modestly; p99 significant for 6-12 minutes; affected customers: customer-phi (critical), babel-ai (high). No data loss. Streaming sessions experienced visible stalls.
Lina: Logged CS case IDs: CS-1123 (phi), CS-1124 (babel). Messaging template ready.
Sam: Action items: (1) Hold rollback of handshake TTL change until postmortem, (2) add warmup capacity headroom to autoscaler policy, (3) create temporary routing fallback runbook.
Maya: I'll open a postmortem ticket and attach logs/traces. Also adding urgent runbook change: increase default handshake TTL to 12s for dedicated pools under warmup heavy class.
Joe: I'll roll a hotfix to kernel init path to reduce cold init by ~40% (low-risk change) and coordinate canary.
Alex: Good. For now keep this thread for live updates. If queue <100 and p99 <1.5s for 10m we'll close.
Maya: 22:12Z update: queue 98, p99 1.4s, streaming stalls minimal. Continue to monitor.
Alex: Thanks all. Paging clear for oncall. We'll handoff to SRE postmortem and runbook owners. :white_check_mark:
Maya: Filed PM-4567 for postmortem + runbook changes. Assigning to Joe and Sam for fix and runbook respectively.
Ron: Ops note: consider pre-warming spare nodes during predicted peak windows. Will follow up with autoscaler tuning RFC.
Lina: Support outreach scheduled in 30m to affected customers.
Joe: I'll post deployment plan for kernel init fix in #eng-runtime tomorrow and include rollback steps.
Alex: Closing thread now — monitoring channel still open. Thanks everyone."
